title: Gunjan Beats Bensalah 5-0 to Win Historic Youth Olympics Boxing Gold
excerpt: The Haryana boxer won the women's 48kg final in Dakar 5-0, becoming the first Indian female boxer to win Youth Olympics gold.
body:
• Gunjan of Haryana beat Algeria's Bouthaina Bensalah 5-0 in the women's 48kg final in Dakar to become the first Indian female boxer to win Youth Olympics gold.
  • She won her quarter-final 5-0 against Mexico's Atena Sofia Juarez Calero and her semi-final 4-1 against Great Britain's Lily Bassett, according to MyKhel and RevSportz.
  • Her gold was India's second boxing gold of the day, after Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei won the men's 50kg title.
  • India's previous Youth Olympics boxing medals were Shiva Thapa's silver and Vikas Krishan's bronze at Singapore 2010.

Gunjan won the women's 48kg gold medal at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Thursday, defeating Algeria's Bouthaina Bensalah 5-0 by unanimous decision in the final. The result makes the Haryana boxer the first Indian female boxer to win a Youth Olympics gold medal, according to MyKhel and RevSportz.

RevSportz reported that all five judges scored the final 30-27 in Gunjan's favour. MyKhel described the performance as commanding, with Gunjan showing composure and control throughout the contest in Dakar, Senegal.

How she reached the final

Gunjan began with a first-round bye, RevSportz reported. In the quarter-finals she beat Mexico's Atena Sofia Juarez Calero 5-0, and in the semi-finals she beat Great Britain's Lily Bassett 4-1.

https://x.com/Olympics/status/2106331834355159125

The semi-final carried a recent history. RevSportz reported that Bassett had defeated Gunjan in the final of the 2026 World Boxing Futures Cup in Bangkok, where Gunjan took silver. In Dakar, Gunjan reversed that result to reach the gold-medal bout.

Gunjan trains at the Manjeet Lohan Boxing Club in Hisar, Haryana, under international professional boxer Vikas Lohan, RevSportz reported.

"This is a historic moment for Indian boxing and Indian sport. Winning two gold medals at the Youth Olympic Games, with India also opening its gold medal account at the Dakar 2026 edition, makes this achievement even more special."

— Ajay Singh, President, Boxing Federation of India, via RevSportz

A double gold day for India

Gunjan's win was India's second boxing gold of the day and of the tournament, RevSportz reported. Earlier, Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei had won the men's 50kg title, making Gunjan only the second Indian boxer to win Youth Olympics gold, according to MyKhel.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dfp3p8fn69f/

Before Dakar, India's only Youth Olympics boxing medals had come at the inaugural Games in Singapore in 2010, MyKhel reported: Shiva Thapa won silver in the men's 54kg and Vikas Krishan won bronze in the men's 60kg. Dakar therefore gave India its first Youth Olympics boxing golds, for both men and women.

RevSportz reported that Gunjan's triumph also ensured India finished its final event at Dakar 2026 with a gold medal, closing the boxing campaign on the podium rather than with a near miss. That closing position matters because both Indian boxers entered in Dakar reached their finals and both won them.

What it means and what comes next

The sources read for this article did not announce Gunjan's next tournament. What they establish is a clear progression in one year: silver at the World Boxing Futures Cup, then Youth Olympics gold after beating the same British opponent who had beaten her in Bangkok.

For young Indian athletes in the diaspora, the result is a concrete marker of Haryana's boxing pipeline reaching the top of the youth podium. Further reporting is in MyKhel and RevSportz.
